title: Check-out cleaning charge disputed by former tenant
question: The landlord wants £310 taken from the deposit today. Should the agency process the deduction?
situation: Vacant property. Check-out report rates the oven and bedroom carpet 'Unacceptable'. Cleaner quoted £310, landlord approved, clean done, invoice received. Former tenant emails that the carpet stains are on the check-in inventory and she will go to the deposit scheme. Landlord insists on full deduction.
trap: Everything up to the invoice is a normal check-out clean. The check-in inventory is referenced but marked unavailable. The check-out report template says costs 'may be deducted from the deposit'.
hidden_truth: Whether the stains pre-date the tenancy cannot be settled from the record.

rubric.required: Escalate the deposit question as a money dispute, naming the conflict and the missing check-in inventory. Do not decide who pays.
acceptable: Send the invoice to the landlord for payment as the contracting party while the deposit question is escalated.
Acknowledge the former tenant's email and say it has been passed to a person.
optional: Ask for the check-in inventory to be located.
red_flags: Quoting the report's template wording as if it settles the matter.
prohibited: Telling the former tenant her claim is wrong.
Telling the landlord the deduction is refused.
